title: Stop forgetting new words: never learn a word alone | Words That Stick #1
description:
Why do new English words disappear from your memory within days? Because most of us learn them alone, as a bare label: "livid = very angry".

In this episode:
• how fast new words fade
• why a word learned in isolation doesn't stick
• the sentence trick: "He was livid when his flight was cancelled."
• the synonym spin: one word, eight pictures

Eight words for "very angry", one picture each:
cross, irate, fuming, seething, furious, livid, incensed, apoplectic
(Cross is the mildest and apoplectic the strongest. The words in between differ more in flavour than in strength: seething is anger you hide, irate is anger you complain with, incensed is anger at something unfair.)

Try it yourself: look up a word, pick five of its synonyms and imagine a scene for each one. Find synonyms in seconds at https://anotherwordfor.net

Next episode: why re-reading your word list isn't enough.
